# Triangles generated by a vertex shader

[Graphics2D::DrawTriangles](../../Siv3D/include/Siv3D/Graphics2D.hpp) draws
triangles whose vertices are generated by a custom vertex shader. It is useful
for animated triangle rows, particles, and shader-generated shapes. The VS
uses `vertexID / 3` to select a triangle and `vertexID % 3` to select its corner.
This is a triangle list, not an instanced draw.

Create the shader and parameter storage before the drawing loop. The paired
[HLSL](../../WindowsDesktop/App/example/shader/hlsl/procedural_triangles.hlsl)
and [MSL](../../macOS/App/example/shader/msl/procedural_triangles.metal) examples
use three Float4 values: origin and size, spacing and rotation (cosine, sine),
and straight RGBA color. Update those parameters and construct a constant-buffer
scope around each group of draws. A single call can generate an entire row of
triangles; separate calls restart the vertex ID and may overlap.

[Page 5 of the custom shader gallery](../../Test/Manual/ScopedCustomShader2D.md)
contains the complete executable example, controls, and expected results. It
compares standard/custom PS, CPU and VS generation, and one call with multiple
triangles against repeated calls with one triangle.

## Shader interface

| Input | HLSL | MSL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertex ID | `SV_VertexID` | `[[vertex_id]]` |
| Standard VS constants | `b0` | `[[buffer(1)]]` |
| Sample's user VS constants | `b2` | `[[buffer(2)]]` |
| Vertex attributes | None | No vertex array at `[[buffer(0)]]` |

Use the [standard VS transform layout](quad-warp.md#vertex-shader-interface)
when generating positions in local drawing coordinates. Preserve homogeneous W
for projective transforms. The examples apply ColorMul before premultiplying
RGB by alpha, and provide the position, PMA color, and UV output expected by the
standard Shape PS. A custom PS may use a different compatible VS output.
Generating clip-space positions directly is also possible; such a VS decides
whether to use the engine's transforms.

Custom constant-buffer snapshots, shader scope restoration, and independent
VS/PS selection follow the existing
[constant-buffer rules](README.md#custom-constant-buffers).
No vertex/index data is allocated or uploaded for these triangles. Renderer2D
still performs its normal initial native buffer bindings; the procedural VS
does not read those buffers. Constant buffers remain available to both stages.

## Command integration

The API retains the vertex-ID drawing model of
[v0.6.16](https://github.com/Siv3D/OpenSiv3D/blob/v0.6.16/Siv3D/src/Siv3D/Graphics2D/SivGraphics2D.cpp#L134-L137).
[SubmitProcedural](../../Siv3D/src/Siv3D/Renderer2D/Renderer2DDrawSubmission.hpp)
selects only the fallback PS; it never replaces the custom VS with an engine VS.
Each backend stores a separate 32-bit vertex count behind its compact command
index. A procedural submission first records any pending indexed draw and state
changes. It never combines calls or advances the indexed-draw cursor.

D3D11 executes `Draw(vertexCount, 0)` with a null input layout and restores the
standard layout within that command. Existing VB/IB bindings and pending batch
updates remain intact. The two input-layout settings are paid only by procedural
draws; ordinary `pushDraw()` and geometry builders have no added mode checks.

Metal executes `drawPrimitives` with vertexStart zero. Both kinds of draw use the
same local pipeline/constant preparation; the existing PSO key does not change.
The command manager's `hasDraws()` includes procedural draws so intermediate
flushes create the required render pass. Indexed offsets, scene clear/load,
MSAA resolve, and frame-slot reuse retain their existing rules.

Do not add input-mode tracking or defer initial buffer binding solely to avoid
a few native state calls. Measure repeated procedural draws and mixed drawing
first, including the effect on ordinary rendering. This feature does not change
the geometry upload path or its write-only cursor boundary.

## Validation and measurement

[Test_Graphics2DDrawTriangles.cpp](../../Test/Test_Graphics2DDrawTriangles.cpp)
checks command order, full-width counts without large GPU submissions, batch
boundaries, constant snapshots, independent PS selection, zero-count batching,
vertex ID reset, and rendered images against ordinary triangles. Rendering
checks cover shader/source lifetime, nested constants, intermediate and empty
flushes, repeated frames, transforms including projective W, colors, blend,
viewport/scissor, culling/wireframe, MSAA, and scene resolution.

Run focused checks and then the full suite using the
[host's workflow](../development/README.md#build-and-test). The focused
correctness filter is `Graphics2DDrawTriangles.*~[benchmark]`. Include the
existing Renderer2D and ConstantBuffer checks when changing command replay.
Windows execution is required to validate D3D11 and the paired HLSL; macOS
execution validates Metal and MSL.

The opt-in `Graphics2DDrawTriangles.cpu_benchmark` compares the same number of
offscreen triangles in ordinary indexed, repeated procedural, one-call
procedural, and mixed drawing. It reports submission time per triangle and
CPU wall time inside Flush, with warmup and percentile reporting. Flush does
not wait for GPU completion, so these are not GPU timings or FPS predictions.
There are no hardware timing assertions in correctness tests.

```sh
CONFIGURATION=Release ./macOS/run-tests.sh '--test-case=Graphics2DDrawTriangles.cpu_benchmark'
CONFIGURATION=Release ./macOS/run-tests.sh '--test-case=Renderer2D.draw_submission_cpu_benchmark'
```

On Windows, use the same test names with the Release Windows runner. Compare
ordinary-drawing results before and after a change on the same idle host;
repeat noisy comparisons. Use native GPU tools separately for GPU duration,
upload bytes, and binding/PSO counts. The gallery remains the place for visual
inspection; automatic pixel comparisons do not establish manual inspection.
